entry.name: The World in One Day
entry.program: main.ts (Node 22, standard library only) validates entry.png against the competition gate (PNG/JPEG signature, 1 MiB cap, 1024x1024 cap, IEND wholeness) and copies it to /output/entry.png, verifying the written bytes by SHA-256. The page itself was drawn at build time by render.py (Pillow, system serif fonts), which is kept in the repository.

stories.facts: The presidents of the United States, China and Russia met together for the first time, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Trump met Putin separately for about 40 minutes — the Kremlin said Ukraine dominated — and Xi Jinping, who described U.S.-China relations as stable and improving. Before the summit Trump said Washington and Beijing could help end the war in Ukraine and shared an interest in oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way summit in Shenzhen

stories.facts: The International Court of Justice delivered its final judgment in The Gambia v. Myanmar, the case brought in November 2019 over the military's 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State, which drove more than 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. The ICJ had never before found a state responsible for genocide; the judgment is final, binding and without appeal. President Yuji Iwasawa read the judgment at a public sitting in The Hague.
stories.headline: World Court delivers judgment in Rohingya genocide case

stories.facts: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on Wednesday evening, above the $70-78 range it had marketed, and upsized the deal to some 980 million shares, raising $81.3 billion — the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's $75 billion listing in June. The price values the company at roughly $1.5 trillion fully diluted; shares begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, after orders reached nearly seven times the shares on offer.
stories.headline: Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO is the largest market debut on record

stories.facts: The International Energy Agency's annual report, published Thursday, describes the Middle East crisis as the greatest threat ever observed to energy security, with consumers absorbing the shock through high prices as other buffers are depleted. In the strait, ADNOC said one crew member of a struck tanker was missing and 11 injured, and UKMTO reported a second tanker hit by an unknown projectile north of Khasab, Oman, its crew safe.
stories.headline: IEA: Hormuz crisis is the greatest threat to energy security ever seen

stories.facts: Crimea's authorities suspended traffic on the bridge linking Russia to the annexed peninsula after a new Ukrainian attack — the third strike on the bridge in a week, following two consecutive nights of strikes that partially destroyed the span, a key supply route and a symbol of President Putin's power.
stories.headline: Ukraine strikes the Crimean Bridge again; traffic suspended

stories.facts: Demonstrations by supporters of Sheikh Hasina's party — Hasina has been sentenced to death — are paralysing regions of Bangladesh. The ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus was set on fire and the residences of two Awami League officials attacked or burned; police recorded dozens of homemade bomb explosions and burned vehicles in at least 28 districts in ten days, and the government deployed paramilitary forces.
stories.headline: Yunus's ancestral home set on fire as violence hits 28 districts

stories.facts: Ministers met in informal session at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Wednesday evening to overcome their differences and adopt a final text; a new draft text is under discussion and a deal remained elusive on Thursday.
stories.headline: Ministers try to unblock COP31 talks in Antalya as a deal stays elusive

stories.facts: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that North Korea is expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung renewed his hope that a resumption of dialogue with Pyongyang would lead to a lasting peace agreement.
stories.headline: IAEA says North Korea is expanding its uranium enrichment
Europe and Hong Kong fall; Brent slips 2.6% to $89.59

stories.facts: Frances Tiafoe saved two set points to beat home favourite Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0 at the Inalpi Arena — his first ATP Finals win — a result that confirmed Carlos Alcaraz, who had beaten Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4, as winner of the Ivan Lendl Group and a semi-finalist.
stories.headline: Tiafoe beat Cobolli 7-6, 6-0 at the ATP Finals in Turin, sending Alcaraz into the semi-finals

stories.facts: 'Chataigniers en fleurs', painted in 1890 in the last two months of Vincent van Gogh's life, was auctioned at Sotheby's in New York for $190.4 million, the most expensive work by the painter ever sold at auction; the sale follows the resolution of a dispute over the painting's Nazi-era ownership history.
stories.headline: Van Gogh's 'Chataigniers en fleurs' sold at Sotheby's New York for $190.4 million, a record for the artist

stories.facts: More than one lakh (100,000) people were evacuated in Odisha as Cyclone Akvan approached landfall near Gopalpur, with red alerts issued for districts in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.
stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan — more than 100,000 people evacuated in Odisha as landfall nears Gopalpur

stories.facts: Israeli President Isaac Herzog asked Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief, to attempt to form the country's next government, choosing him over sitting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
stories.headline: President Herzog asked former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, not Netanyahu, to try to form a government
